items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names in the core logic (`a`, `b`, `s`, `n`, `cap`, `top`). The language-switching trick (`#if 0` / `""" "` / `#endif`) has no comment in the file, although the conventions ask for one. The bignum code has a short comment.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is compact and `main` is about 27 lines, but `#include <string.h>` is never used (dead include). All the C logic sits in `main` with no `fib` helper. The bignum code adds complexity the task did not ask for.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No input validation: `atol(argv[1])` accepts junk and negative values. A large negative n makes `(size_t)(n/40+2)` wrap to a huge size. `calloc` is never checked for NULL before `a[0] = 0`. Magic constants: `1000000000u`, `n / 40 + 2`.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: f(0), f(1) and large n are correct and iterative in both languages, and C is exact beyond 93. But a missing argument prints 0 with exit 0, non-numeric C input prints 0, and negative input in C is undefined. Argument errors never give a non-zero exit.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: Works with exactly the two given commands. After the `""" "` / `" """` fix, gcc showed no warnings. Each run prints only the number, and both outputs matched for n = 0 to 1000.
